title: The union merger and why members left
summary: Cotton recalls vague conflict over merging Black and white locals and says the union does little, while his government pension makes him independent.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Real number three with Lawrence Cotton on December 10, 1996. Weren't there some real problems with the union? I mean, the black union, when it was black and when it was split?

Oh, when they were trying to decide whether they were going to merge. It was some kind of conflict. I don't know what it was. I really wasn't concerned about it because I think I was going in and out of town at the time. So it really didn't concern me too much.
Was there a problem with the merger at that time when they did merge?

I think, I don't know. I think they tried to see who was established first. Was it the Caucasian or was it the blacks? Mm-hmm. But I don't know what happened. But anyway, they finally merged, but there were more Caucasians than there were blacks. Sure. Mm-hmm. So then they've just put in stipulated that they have to at least have one or two blacks on the staff. On the board? On the board or something, yeah. On the board staff. They have to at least allow that. Otherwise, it'd be wiped out. Mm-hmm. You know, you could be completely wiped out. So that's all that, in fact, I have been to a meeting. I can't tell you the last meeting I've been to. Mm-hmm. Because most of the time, they have the meetings, I'd be working.
So the general consensus is the union here, well, in the last so many years, it hasn't been very powerful. I mean, it just hasn't.
It hasn't really worked. It seems in the best interest of the musicians.
A lot of people have stopped being in the union because, I mean, they're not doing anything for you.
You know, they used to have projects that they'd throw your way, you know, when you leaned in the years, well, nothing happened, you know.

But see, I'm not in a category, not that I'm bragging, but about me working for the government. And I retired for the government, so now I'm on my own place. I can be independent about who I play with, if I want to play, you see. I can be charged about who I play with, you see. Yeah. But there are some guys, from check to check, from day to day, that's where they live. They never looked out for tomorrow, for the next day. But that didn't happen with me, you see, because I always planned on what's going to happen down the line. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
